Part of #101. Found while building #108 (PR #121).

`packages/cloudflare/src/SubmissionWorker.ts` (~:247) serves `POST /my-answers`: given an Edit key **or its stored hash** (body `editKeyHash`/`edit_key_hash`, or the same names in the query string), it looks up `submission_index` in D1 and returns that Submission's answers via `getMyAnswers`. Nothing in `apps/` calls it; the history page (ADR 0017) reads answers from the member's browser instead.

Accepting the hash means anyone who reads `submission_index` (an operator, a D1 export) can fetch answers without the member's key, and query-string parameters are the kind of value ADR 0005 keeps out of URLs.

Decide: remove the route and `getMyAnswers` if no flow needs it, or accept only the raw Edit key in the POST body. Add a privacy test either way (ADR 0005, A1–A10).

Issue #124: `redact("3 0301234567 4 0301234567", [])` returns the input unchanged; two German landline numbers leak (ADR 0009: when in doubt, redact).

Root cause (verified): in `packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.ts`, step 4 uses `result.replace(GERMAN_PHONE_PATTERN, cb)`. The pattern is greedy and matches the whole span `0301234567 4 0301234567` as one match with 20 significant digits; the callback keeps any match outside 7-12 digits, so the whole span is left. The generic rule then misses each half (a 10-digit run has no separator; the lone `4` cannot form a 2-5 digit group).

Fix (decided): replace the `.replace` in step 4 with a small `redactGermanPhones(text)` exec loop (like `redactGenericPhones`, fresh `new RegExp(GERMAN_PHONE_PATTERN.source, "g")`). For each match:
- significant digits (existing `germanSignificantDigits`) < 7: keep, continue.
- 7..12: replace with `[phone]`.
- > 12 (two or more numbers run together): find the SHORTEST prefix of the match that ends right before a separator character (space, `/`, `-`) and has >= 7 significant digits (groups are at most 6 digits, so that prefix has <= 12). Replace that prefix with `[phone]` and set `pattern.lastIndex` to the end of the prefix so the rest of the text is scanned again (the rest starts with the separator, so the lookbehind works). If no such prefix exists (e.g. an unseparated run of 13+ digits), redact the whole match as `[phone]` (when in doubt, redact).
